contexts.text: The things of the will are here signified by the wild beast (or wild) of that earth ().
Things which are lower in man, and which derive more from the body, are called the wild beasts of that earth, and are cupidities and pleasures. AC 46:2, ill.
Distinction between wild beasts of the earth, and... wild beasts of the field.
See Beast. AC 47.
The Natural of (the spiritual man) is here signified by the wild beast of the earth... () to which there was given for food the vegetable and the green of the herb. Illustrated.
The serpent was more subtle than any wild beast of the field... ()... The wild beast of the field, here, as before, = every affection of the external man. AC 242. AC 245. AC 246., ill. AE 739:9.
Their ferine nature. Treated of.
Thy wild beast shall dwell in it () = that the affection of good [will do so]. ( = the regenerate man. AC 908:2.)

That he should live like a wild beast. Signified. He lives like a wild beast when the internal man is so separated from the external that it does not operate into it, except in a very general way. For, that man is man he has through the internal man from the Lord; but that he is a wild beast, he has from the external man, which, separated from the internal, is in itself nothing but a wild beast: it has a like nature, cupidities, appetites, phantasies, and sensations. The organic things are also similar.
In what precedes it has treated... first of those who lived like wild-animals (or wild-things), and at last became spiritual men...

The wild beast after its kind () = all spiritual good; and the beast after its kind = all natural good... Thus wild beast involves what is of higher worth and excellence than beast. The reason is, that in the Hebrew the term means also an animal in which there is a living soul. And so here, it does not mean a wild beast, but an animal in which there is a living soul; for [in the Hebrew] it is the same word.
(All flesh expired)... as to wild beast () = the pleasures in their persuasions (did so).
(God remembered)... every wild beast () = that (the Lord is merciful to) everything...

Wild beast, in the Word, is taken in two senses for those which are alive, because, in the Hebrew, the terra means what is alive: but as, in their humiliation, the Most Ancients acknowledged themselves to be wild beasts, the term came to mean also the things with man which are dead. By wild beast, here, is signified both what is alive and what is dead in one complex, as is usually the case with man after temptation. Explained. (Compare AC 908.)
Deliver not the soul of Thy turtledove unto the wild beast () = the life of faith to those who have no charity. ( = to the falsity of evil. AE 388:16.)
Every wild beast that is with thee of all flesh () = everything vivified in the man of this Church. For wild beast is predicated of Noah, that is, of the man of this Church now regenerated.
Thus the same word means What is alive, and wild beast. Illustrated.
Every wild beast of the forest is Mine... and the wild beasts of My field are with Me () = the regenerated man, thus what is living in him.

I will make a covenant for them with the wild beast of the field () = with those who are to be regenerated. (Compare AC 9182:6.) ( = with the affection of the Knowledges of truth. AE 650:24.) ( = with the affection of truth and good. AE 701:20.)
So much does fera = what is living, that the Cherubs or Angels seen by Ezekiel are called the four living creatures.
That, in the contrary sense, fera = what is not living, that is, a savage wild beast. Illustrated.
The Jews... were so cruel, and such wild beasts, that... This shows what a wild beast man is.
That every wild-animal () = ... the goods of the internal man. Explained.
What is more agreeable than to hear that one may be saved, even if he lives like a fierce wild beast?
When born, man is the lowest among all wild beasts and beasts.

Wild beasts are never so (savage as man in his native state). Those which are fierce and rapacious harm others only to defend themselves, (or) to appease their hunger... AC 1738. SE 2026, General article. AC 5393. SE 1063.
To kill animals and eat their flesh, was, to them, (to act) like wild beasts... But when men began to be even more ferocious than wild beasts, they began to (do this)...

At the hand of every wild beast () = from all that is violent in man... For, in the contrary sense, wild beast = what is like a wild beast, thus whatever is ferine in man... and therefore it = one who is violent, that is, one who inflicts violence on charity; for he is like a wild beast. From love and charity a man is a man; but from hatred, revenge, and cruelty he is a wild beast.
Every wild beast of the earth () = his derivative lower intellectual and voluntary things... These exterior things are scientifics and pleasures...

Of all that go out of the ark, even every wild-animal of the earth () = the men of the Church, (and) the man outside the Church... The wild-animal of the earth is here mentioned a second time, (which shows) that something else is meant by it... (namely) all in the universe who are outside the Church.

When things living are not signified by wild beast, it = things which are lower and which partake more or less of a ferine nature, in accordance with what is being treated of. When it is predicated of what is in man, the wild beast of the earth = the lower things, which are those of the external man and the body, as just before... But when it is predicated of an entire society... the wild beast of the earth = those who are not of the Church, because they are lower. Further illustrated.
Men (now) treat one another like wild beasts...
Otherwise, man is a wild beast.
They give drink to every wild-animal of the fields () = goods. ( = those who live thence. AC 2702:10.) ( = those in the good of the Church. AE 483:7.) ( = to the affections of truth. AE 1100:9.)
I will cause evil wild beasts to cease out of the land () = that the cupidities of evil will cease.

That which is torn () = the evil which is from the falsity that is injected by the evil [Spirits] who are the wild beasts in the forest which tear; for in the Word the internals are compared to wild beasts.

An evil wild beast hath devoured him () = a lie from a life of cupidities; for a wild beast = affection and cupidity. For, in the genuine sense, a wild beast = what is alive; and therefore an evil wild beast = a life of cupidities. ( = that the cupidities of evil have extinguished it. AC 4776.)
The wild beasts of the field () = the evil which destroys the Church as to faith in the Lord. ( = Falsities. AE 388:4.)
The man (thus) destroys the human in himself, and makes himself a wild beast... When such are looked at by the Angels, they appear... like wild beasts.
The evil wild beast = falsities from evils. Illustrated.
In the spiritual sense, wild beasts which tear = the evils of cupidities and the derivative falsities; and, in the other life, these are represented by wild beasts.
He thus puts off the human nature, and puts on a ferine one; for wild beasts look downwards...
By the evil wild beast (which is the third of the four kinds of vastations and punishments that are mentioned in the Word) is signified the punishment of the evil which is from falsity. Illustrated.
(Some of the inhabitants of Venus) are almost ferine... SE 3346. Described.
That there have been people of such a ferine nature in this Earth also. Illustrated.
When their external bonds are taken away... and they are left to their cupidities, they are like wild beasts...
If the good of the love of self and of the world... be the soul of a man, he is not a man, but a wild beast; and, in the other life, in the light of Heaven, he appears as a wild beast...
The wild beast of the field = life from good.

What they leave, the wild beast of the field shall eat () = (conjunction) through these with those who are in the delights of external truth... For beasts-bestiae = affections of truth and good... but wild beasts, such affections as are of the most external truth; for, relatively to the internal affections, these are wild beasts, for they are affections of sensuous things, which are called pleasures and delights...

Lest the wild beast of the field multiply against thee () = an afflux of falsities from the delights of the loves of self and of the world... For beasts-bestiae of various kinds = good and evil affections; and therefore wild beasts = affections of what is false which originate from (these) delights; and, in the other life, these affections are represented by wild beasts, such as panthers, tigers, wild boars, wolves, and bears. Moreover, these affections are like wild beasts; for those who are in these loves are in evils and the derivative falsities of every kind, and they regard and treat their associates as wild beasts would do. AE 388:7. AE 650:59. AE 650:60.
That wild beast = falsity and evil from the loves of self and the world. Illustrated.
As wild beast = what is false, and as this is from a double origin wild beast, in the Word, - also the upright gentiles. Illustrated.

As such think insanely, because from lowest things, they are called the wild beast of the reed (). See AE 388:13. AE 439:5. AE 627:13. ( = the cupidity of falsity which is from the scientifics of the sensuous man. AE 654:54.)
If he is wild and untamed, he is called a tear or a wolf.
Dark forests in which wander malignant Spirits, like wild beasts.
a. [end]. I then said. So that you are like wild beasts. On hearing this, fury seized them ...
The Angel said. All these wild beasts that you have seen are not wild beasts, but correspondences... of the cupidities in which are the people we are about to visit...
Those (devils) were seen as various kinds of wild beasts, with fierce eyes.
The external (of such a one) is human, and his internal ferine.

(Such) thereby put off the Human, and put on the Ferine, and become like beasts foxes in cunning, wolves in fierceness, etc... In the Spiritual World they appear at a distance like these wild beasts. So their love of evil figures itself.
If he closes the lowest natural degree as to its Spiritual, he becomes, as to his love, like a wild beast...

This (diabolical love of self) is the cause of its cupidities appearing... at a distance like various species of wild beasts; some, like foxes and leopards; some like wolves and tigers; and some like crocodiles and venomous serpents.
And the earth was cleared of those wild-creatures (that is, of the birds of night, locusts, and spectres).
(Otherwise) what is ferine would enter men... so that they could not be restrained by any laws...

The combat of the Lord with Hell may be compared... to a fight with the wild beasts of the whole world, and their slaughter and subjugation... Moreover infernal Spirits are described in the Word as wild beasts. They are meant in , by the wild beastswith which the Lord wasfor forty days.
Like robbers who... when they return into the forests are like wild beasts.

At a distance (such) appear like wild beasts of every kind = tigers, leopards, wolves, foxes, dogs, crocodiles, serpents... and when they see gentle animals in the representative forms, they rush at them...

The concupiscences of the flesh... are exactly like those of beasts-bestiarum, and therefore, in themselves, are ferine... Therefore, in proportion as anyone indulges (these) concupiscences, he is a beast-bestia, and a wild beast.
No one can approach another who keeps a leopard and a panther... unless he first removes these wild beasts. TCR 436.
With two... faces; one ferine, the other... human.
Inwardly, he is a beast; nay, a wild beast...
I have seen evil moral men (when their external was put off) like wild beasts; their fierce eyes fixed on the neighbour... See AE 388:2.
Regarded in himself, the natural man... differs not from the nature of beasts-bestiarum: he is in like manner wild and untamed = that is, as to the will...
If the will were not held in check through the understanding, the man... from the ferine nature implanted in him, would plunder and slaughter...
That fierce creatures with many feet, such insects, for instance, = the more insane devils. General article. SE 1915., Example(s).

The life of evil Spirits is not different from that of wild beasts; for they act from instinct, and know no otherwise than that they live a life just like wild animals... The ferine life of evil Spirits is worse in this respect = that they are carried by their instinct against what is good and true; which they derive from the fact... that they have been born men.
As he was of such a ferine nature, he was despatched into the Hell of such. SE 4634.
All said that they are no longer men, but are like wild beasts; for they had put off the human nature by bursting asunder and profaning the society [which comes into existence by] marriage.

Evil wild beasts (shall) cease out of the land () = that there should not be evil affections and concupiscences, which destroy the Church. AE 365:14. AE 365:27. AE 388:7. ( = exemption from the cupidity for falsity. AE 650:58.)
No lion shall be there, neither shall a ravenous one of the wild beasts be found therein () = that there shall be no falsity destroying truth, nor evil destroying good. AE 388:10. AE 650:54.

And by the wild beasts of the earth () = evils of life, which are the cupidities and derivative Falsities that originate from the love of self and of the world, and which devastate all things of the Church with man. (See AR 323, where beast in the same passage is bestia in the Latin.)
That wild beasts, here, = in special, evils of life, is evident from the series... Explained.
That evil wild beasts = the (above mentioned) cupidities and Falsities; and also, in the opposite sense, the affections of truth that vivify all things of the Church. Illustrated.
The wild beast of the field () = the derivative Falsities and evil cupidities. AE 403:5.
The evil wild beast = the cupidities which destroy good affections. Illustrated.
The evil wild beast in the land () = cupidities; and the wild beast of the field () = Falsities.
The wild beast of the field shall rend them () = cupidities and Falsities. ( = that they will be destroyed by falsities from evil. AE 781:14.)
Every wild beast of the nation () = the falsity of evil. ( = the affections of falsity. AE 650:56.)
Every wild beast of the field shall be upon his branches () = that then there will be... evils of affection. AE 650:28. ( = affections of falsity. AE 654:36.)
The evils signified by the wild beast of the field () are evils of life, which are the cupidities that originate from the love of self and of the world.
The wild beast of the earth () = the derivative affections of evil.
The wild beast of the field () = evils from falsities.
The wild beast () = the evil of falsity.
The evil wild beast () = the deprivation of (the good of love and the truth of faith) through the evils of the love of self and of the world.

The evil wild beast means all noxious beasts that seize and rend asunder good animals... They are lions, tigers, panthers, wild-boars, wolves, dragons, serpents, and many others. That these wild beasts, and the evil wild beast in general = the cupidities that originate from the love of self and of the world, from which come all the evils of life and the falsities of doctrine, is from correspondence, as is evident from the appearances in the Spiritual World; for there all the cupidities of evil and of falsity appear as wild beasts of various kinds; and moreover those from whom such things appear are like wild beasts; for their greatest delight is to attack and destroy the good.

It shall now be shown that wild beasts, in the Word, = also the affections of truth and good... The reason (of this signification) is that the word in the Original Language means life; for fera in that language is chajah, which means life; and the very life of the spiritual man consists in the affection of truth and good; so that when fera is mentioned in this good sense, it ought rather to be changed into and called animal which means a living soul. When fera is mentioned in this sense, the idea that adheres to the word fera in the Latin language must be entirely set aside; for in that language an idea of what is wild and ferocious adheres to the word fera... In the Hebrew language it is different, for there fera means life; and a living soul, or animal, in general. In this sense chajah or fera cannot be called beast; because, in the Word, fera and bestia are sometimes mentioned together, when fera = the affection of truth, and bestia the affection of good. As fera, or chajah, in this (good) sense = the affection, of truth and of good. Eve... is called Chavah. (See ). And the four animals (in Ezekiel) are also called chajah, in the plural; and as an idea of what is wild and ferocious adheres to the word fera, the translators have said animalia...
Animals that may be eaten, such as lambs sheep, etc... and also those which are not to be eaten are also called by the general word ferae... Illustrated.
The animals that were sacrificed are also called ferae. Illustrated.
That fera = the affection of truth and good, Illustrated.

In , by bestias et feras are meant lambs, sheep, goats, oxen, horses, donkeys, etc.; and not lions, bears, wild-boars, and the like rapacious wild beasts; so that by the ferae, here, are meant the domestic animals which are useful, and which = affections of truth and of good.
Praise Jehovah... ye wild-animal and every beast () = the affections of truth and of good.
Thy wild-animal shall dwell therein () = that the affections of truth and of good (will dwell in the Church)... For no ferocious wild beast can dwell in (it).
The wild-animal of the field () = the affections of truth. ( = the affections of scientifics. AE 650:27.)
See Beast.

When it is said the wild beast of the earth there is meant the wild beast which devours animals and men; but when it is said the wild-animal of the field, there is meant the wild-animal which consumes what has been sown; so that the wild beast of the earth = the things which destroy the goods of the Church; and the wild-animal of the field, the things which destroy the truths of the Church. Explained.
The wild beast of the field () = the affection and the cupidity of falsity and of evil. ( = affections from scientifics. AE 650:41.)

In many passages it is sometimes said bestia and sometimes fera; and by fera is not meant fera in the sense in which there is contained the idea of wild things; for, in the Hebrew, fera is derived from a word which means life; and therefore in some passages instead of fera it is better to say animal... But still there is a careful distinction made in the Word between bestiae and ferae; by bestiae being signified the affections of the natural man which are of his will; and by ferae, the affections of the natural man which are of his understanding...
The wild-animal of the forest () = the affection of scientifics.
Both small and great wild beasts () = various affections.
Every wild beast of the field () = all, in whatever kind of affection of good they may be.

All in the Church who are in truths from good... are meant by the wild beasts of the fields of the Lord Jehovih ()... And the gentiles outside the Church are signified by the wild beast in the forest.
In the opposite sense... wild = the cupidities of falsifying and thus destroying the truths of the Church. Illustrated.
The wild beast of the earth shall not devour them () = that (the man of the Church shall not be destroyed by) the cupidities of falsity.
Assemble every wild beast of the field, come ye to devour () = the cupidities of destroying the truths of the Church by means of falsities.
A crouching place for the wild beast () = the state of a vastated Church as to truths.

As wild beast = the cupidities of falsity from evil; and birds, the derivative thoughts and reasonings... therefore, where the vastation of the Church is treated of, it is said that they shall be given to the wild beasts and birds to be devoured. Illustrated. AE 654:52.
Such is the ferine nature of those in Hell.
I will cause the evil wild beast to cease () = peace from the infestation of what is evil and false from Hell.

Speak unto... every wild beast of the field, Assemble yourselves and come... () = the establishment of the Church among the gentiles... every wild beast of the field = all who are in the affection of good and the understanding of truth.
